course.title: AP Precalculus
course.description: Build the function toolkit that calculus depends on: how quantities change together, polynomial and rational functions, exponential and logarithmic models, and trigonometric and polar functions.
course.previewDescription: Study how outputs change with inputs, then use polynomial, rational, exponential, logarithmic, and trigonometric functions to describe patterns and build models.

unit.title: Trigonometric and Polar Functions
unit.description: Model periodic phenomena with sine, cosine, and tangent, use inverse trigonometric functions and identities, and describe how polar functions change.

topic.title: Sinusoidal Functions
topic.summary: Sinusoidal functions as transformations of sin θ, with period, frequency, amplitude, and midline, plus the concavity of their graphs and the symmetry that makes sine odd and cosine even.

questions.prompt: A sinusoidal function has a maximum value of 9 and a minimum value of 1. What are the amplitude and midline of its graph?
choiceExplanations: 8 is the full difference between maximum and minimum; the amplitude is half of it.
The midline is the average of 9 and 1, not half their difference.
Half the difference is 4; the average is 5.
This takes the full difference and uses half the difference for the midline.
questions.distinguisher: Amplitude halves the difference; midline averages the values.

questions.prompt: A sinusoidal function has a period of 4. What is its frequency?
questions.explanation: Period and frequency are reciprocals, so the frequency is 1/4: one quarter of a cycle per unit of input.
choiceExplanations: 4 is the period itself.
π/2 = 2π/4 confuses the frequency with the value b in sin(bθ), which Topic 3.6 relates to the period.
8 is twice the period.
The reciprocal of the period 4.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is true for all real numbers θ?
questions.explanation: The graph of y = cos θ has reflective symmetry over the y-axis, so cosine is an even function: cos(−θ) = cos θ.
choiceExplanations: That is the odd-function rule, which holds for sine, not cosine.
Cosine is even.
Sine is odd, so sin(−θ) = −sin θ.
π is half the period; cos(θ + π) = −cos θ.
questions.distinguisher: Cosine is even, sine is odd.

questions.prompt: The graph of a sinusoidal function g is shown. What is the equation of the midline of the graph of g?

stimulusBlocks.caption: Graph of y = g(x)
stimulusBlocks.alt: A wave that oscillates between a maximum of 3 and a minimum of −5.

questions.explanation: The maximum is 3 and the minimum is −5, so the midline is y = (3 + (−5))/2 = −1.
choiceExplanations: The average of 3 and −5 is −1.
4 is the amplitude, (3 − (−5))/2, not the midline.
y = 0 is the x-axis, the midline of sin θ and cos θ, but this graph is shifted down.
questions.distinguisher: Average the maximum and minimum; don't halve their difference.

questions.prompt: Which of the following expressions is equal to cos θ for all real numbers θ?
questions.explanation: The sine and cosine functions are both sinusoidal functions, with cos θ = sin(θ + π/2).
choiceExplanations: sin(θ − π/2) = −cos θ; the shift is in the wrong direction.
Shifting the sine graph π/2 to the left gives the cosine graph.
Adding π/2 to the output moves the graph up, not sideways.
Multiplying the input changes the period, not the starting point.
questions.distinguisher: Add π/2 inside the sine, not subtract it.

questions.prompt: On which of the following intervals is the graph of y = sin θ concave up?
questions.explanation: On π < θ < 2π the graph of y = sin θ is below its midline y = 0, where it is concave up.
choiceExplanations: On 0 < θ < π the graph is above the midline and concave down.
The graph changes concavity at θ = π, inside this interval.
Below the midline, the graph is concave up.
The graph changes concavity at θ = 0, inside this interval.
questions.distinguisher: For sine, concavity changes where the graph crosses y = 0.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a point of inflection of the graph of y = cos θ?
questions.explanation: The graph of y = cos θ changes from concave down to concave up where it crosses its midline y = 0, at θ = π/2.
choiceExplanations: (0, 1) is a maximum; the graph is concave down on both sides.
(π, −1) is a minimum, where the graph is concave up on both sides.
At π/4 the graph is still above the midline and concave down.
The graph crosses the midline here and changes concavity.
questions.distinguisher: Inflection points of sinusoidal graphs are on the midline, not at the extremes.

questions.prompt: A sinusoidal function f has a maximum value of 7 at x = 1, and its next minimum value, −1, occurs at x = 4. Which of the following is true?
choices: The period is 3, and the midline is y = 3.
The period is 6, and the midline is y = 4.
The period is 6, and the midline is y = 3.
The period is 3, and the amplitude is 8.
questions.explanation: From a maximum to the next minimum is half a cycle, so the period is 2(4 − 1) = 6. The midline is y = (7 + (−1))/2 = 3.
choiceExplanations: 3 units is only half a cycle, from a maximum to a minimum.
4 is the amplitude, (7 − (−1))/2, not the midline.
Half a cycle is 3 units, so a full cycle is 6; the average of 7 and −1 is 3.
The period is 6 and the amplitude is 4.
questions.distinguisher: Maximum to next minimum is half a period.

questions.prompt: Which of the following describes the symmetry of the graph of y = sin θ?
choices: Reflective symmetry over the y-axis, so sine is even
Reflective symmetry over the x-axis, so sine is an odd function
Rotational symmetry about the origin, so sine is an odd function
Rotational symmetry about the origin, so sine is even
questions.explanation: The graph of y = sin θ has rotational symmetry about the origin and is therefore an odd function.
choiceExplanations: Reflective symmetry over the y-axis describes cosine, which is even.
A function's graph cannot be symmetric over the x-axis unless it is y = 0.
Rotational symmetry about the origin means sin(−θ) = −sin θ.
Rotational symmetry about the origin makes a function odd, not even.
questions.distinguisher: Odd goes with the origin; even goes with the y-axis.

questions.prompt: The air pressure of a musical note is modeled by a sinusoidal function of time with a frequency of 440 cycles per second. What is the period of the function?
questions.explanation: Period and frequency are reciprocals, so the period is 1/440 second, about 0.00227 second per cycle.
choiceExplanations: 440 is the frequency, the number of cycles in one second.
The reciprocal of 440 cycles per second.
2π/440 brings in the period of sin θ, but the period is simply the reciprocal of the frequency.
This is neither the frequency nor its reciprocal.
